findings.title: Applet progress is loaded and saved over plain HTTP
findings.entry_point: In applet mode, selecting Play invokes the progress-loading request; the response is attacker-controlled network input. ApoSimpleSudokuApplet.java:25-26 enables applet mode, ApoSimpleSudokuMenu.java:111-115 handles Play, and ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.java:133-137 starts the load.
findings.sink: ApoHelp.loadData/saveData opens an HttpURLConnection at ApoHelp.java:424-425 and 452-455. The supplied base URL is the literal "http://www.apo-games.de/apoSudoku/" at ApoSimpleSudokuConstants.java:28.
findings.data_path: ApoSimpleSudokuApplet.init (ApoSimpleSudokuApplet.java:36-46) -> Play/P -> ApoSimpleSudokuPanel.setLevelChooser (ApoSimpleSudokuPanel.java:159-167) -> ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.init/loadCookies (ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.java:65-72,133-149) -> ApoHelp.loadData (ApoHelp.java:446-465). On completion, ApoSimpleSudokuGame.checkWin (ApoSimpleSudokuGame.java:176-179) -> ApoSimpleSudokuPanel.solveLevel (ApoSimpleSudokuPanel.java:207-208) -> solveLevel/saveCookies (ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.java:159-178) -> ApoHelp.saveData (ApoHelp.java:419-438).
findings.attack_scenario: A network attacker intercepts the cleartext request when an applet user opens Play. The attacker reads the submitted solved-level list or replaces the load response with "0,1,...,30,". The parser adds those values at ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.java:144-149 and the renderer marks every level solved at lines 273-282. The practical impact is disclosure or corruption of game progress and cosmetic cheating; all level buttons are already visible at lines 52-63, so this does not unlock privileged functionality.
findings.preconditions: The game must be run through the included JApplet entry point on a legacy applet-capable runtime, the user must open the level chooser or finish a level, and apo-games.de HTTP traffic must reach a malicious server or be interceptable. The ordinary desktop main path sets applet=false at ApoSimpleSudokuMain.java:30 and does not execute these requests.
findings.validation_plan: Run the applet entry point in a legacy appletviewer or equivalent harness through an intercepting HTTP proxy. Click Play and verify a request to http://www.apo-games.de/apoSudoku/cookies.php. Return "0,1,2,...,30," as the first response line and confirm that every level receives the solved overlay. Then solve a level and confirm that the cleartext request body contains SET, apoSudoku_level, and the progress list.

findings.title: Unbounded HTTP response line can hang or exhaust the game process
findings.code_excerpt:
BufferedReader iStream = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(con.getInputStream()));
			retVal = iStream.readLine();
findings.entry_point: A malicious apo-games.de server or HTTP interceptor controls the cookies.php response consumed by ApoHelp.loadData at ApoHelp.java:464-465 and saveData at lines 435-436.
findings.sink: BufferedReader.readLine at ApoHelp.java:465 and 436 reads without a response-size bound. The URL connections created at lines 425 and 454 have no connect or read timeout configured.
findings.data_path: Applet Play -> ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.init creates the loading thread (ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.java:65-72) -> loadCookies (lines 133-149) -> ApoHelp.loadData -> readLine (ApoHelp.java:464-465). A second synchronous route is puzzle completion -> checkWin (ApoSimpleSudokuGame.java:176-179) -> saveCookies (ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.java:159-178) -> ApoHelp.saveData -> readLine (ApoHelp.java:435-436).
findings.attack_scenario: For the load route, the attacker streams a very large response without a newline; readLine keeps accumulating data and can consume the shared JVM heap. Alternatively, the attacker sends millions of comma-terminated integers: the unbounded loop at ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.java:144-149 stores every value in solvedLevels. For the save route, accepting the connection but never completing the response blocks the game-loop thread after a level is solved.
findings.preconditions: Applet mode must be used and the HTTP endpoint must be malicious or intercepted. Opening Play reaches the load route; completing a previously unrecorded level reaches the synchronous save route.
findings.validation_plan: Route www.apo-games.de to a controlled HTTP server and run the applet with a small heap such as -Xmx64m. On the Play request, continuously send "128," without a newline and monitor heap growth until an OutOfMemoryError or process failure occurs. Separately, return an empty initial progress line, solve level 1, accept the save request without sending a response, and confirm through a thread dump and frozen rendering that the game loop is blocked in BufferedReader.readLine.

findings.title: Dormant URL class loader instantiates arbitrary external classes
findings.entry_point: There is no untrusted in-game entry point. The only input surface is the public ApoClassLoader(path, classname) constructor at ApoClassLoader.java:19-22, which currently has no call site elsewhere in the 43-file variant.
findings.sink: getMyClass converts the supplied path into a local or remote URL at ApoClassLoader.java:64-69, loads the supplied class name at line 73, and executes its initialization/constructor through newInstance at line 75.
findings.data_path: Theoretical only: an embedding or future caller supplies path and classname -> constructor stores them (ApoClassLoader.java:19-22,36-37,52-53) -> getMyClass selects File.toURL or new URL (lines 62-69) -> URLClassLoader.loadClass (line 73) -> Class.newInstance (line 75). ApoSimpleSudokuGameComponent.java:29-40 defines a .class chooser, but its getters at lines 62-94 are never called and there is no showOpenDialog/getSelectedFile-to-loader path.
findings.attack_scenario: Not exploitable through the shipped game. If reused code later passes an attacker-selected directory or HTTP base URL and class name, the attacker places a class there whose static initializer or public constructor runs commands; getMyClass then executes it with the game's JVM privileges.
findings.preconditions: A new caller must be added or an embedding application must invoke ApoClassLoader with attacker-controlled path and classname. Merely placing a .class file beside the current game is insufficient because this variant never calls the loader.
findings.validation_plan: Create evil.Payload with a public no-argument constructor that writes a marker file, compile it under a served directory, and use a small harness to set ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true and invoke new ApoClassLoader("http://127.0.0.1:8000/", "evil.Payload").getMyClass(). The marker confirms code execution. Then verify that normal desktop and applet UI operation never requests Payload, confirming the finding remains theoretical in this variant.

notes: All 43 files under the target root are Java source files and were searched for security-sensitive APIs and call sites. The ordinary desktop path is offline: ApoSimpleSudokuMain.java:30 selects applet=false, while both progress-network methods are guarded by B_APPLET at ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.java:134 and 160. Levels are built from source literals rather than external files (ApoSimpleSudokuLevelMake.java:5-69). The .class/.rep/.skunk chooser scaffolding at ApoSimpleSudokuGameComponent.java:29-40 and 62-94, abstract file/URL operations at ApoIO.java:31-105, and external-image branch at ApoImage.java:90-94 have no game call sites. ApoHelp.getMd5Digest defines MD5 at ApoHelp.java:313-318 but is never called, so there is no reachable weak integrity check. No ObjectInputStream, System.load/native declaration, save_highscore.php/save_level.php/get_level.php endpoint, embedded credential, or reachable user-controlled file parser/path sink occurs in this variant.
